name: Demta
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Suharyanto. 2016. Kekerabatan bahasa-bahasa di kawasan utara Kabupaten Jayapura. Kibas Cenderawasih 13(2): 187-198.
sources.note: Lexicostatistics only (Demta shares <6% cognates with Sentani/Tabla/Yokari/Tevera Pew, has no dialects); no phonology, no mention of stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-213 (add name Sowari to [dmy]), submitted by Randy Lebold, SIL.
sources.note: Nothing; only names the source 'Survey Report on the Sowari (Demta) Language. Draft survey report' from the SIL rapid appraisal of March 2006 and explains Sowari = autonym, Demta = outsiders' name.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and langdoc bibliography for demt1241 (9 refs: Wafom 2002; Smits & Voorhoeve 1994; Voorhoeve 1975; Galis 1955; Cowan 1952, 1953, 1957; Kim 2006; ISO CR 2007-213).
sources.note: No phonology or grammar of Demta is listed; the one 'specific_feature' item is Wafom's syntax report. Cowan 1952/1957, Galis 1955, Voorhoeve 1975, Smits & Voorhoeve 1994 are wordlist/overview items.

sources.citation: Cowan, H.K.J. 1953. Voorlopige resultaten van een ambtelijk taalonderzoek in Nieuw-Guinea. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. 48 pp.
sources.note: p. 2: Demta listed as no. 17 of the north-coast non-Austronesian languages; 'De taal van Demta kon (nog) niet nader bij enige groep worden ingedeeld, doch zij vertoont punten van overeenkomst met het Sentani.' Nothing on klemtoon/accent for Demta.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Warry' (Kampung Ambora, Distrik Demta, Kabupaten Jayapura, Provinsi Papua).
sources.note: Location and dialectometry only (81-100% difference from Tarfia, Kemtuk, Gresi); no phonology.

sources.citation: Wafom, Yunus et al. 2002 [2003]. Sintaksis bahasa Demta: laporan penelitian. Jayapura: Universitas Cenderawasih / Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Companion Cenderawasih report; its introduction may summarise Fautngil 2000's phonology (including stress); syntax itself unlikely to help.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no Harvard e-access found (also: publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Overview of the Sentani family; snippet shows Foley treats Sowari as wordlists-only, so it would at most confirm the absence of a description, not supply a stress rule.

sources.citation: Normawati (ed.). 2007. Profil penelitian kebahasaan dan kesastraan Papua. Jayapura: Balai Bahasa Jayapura. 142 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Abstracts every Balai Bahasa/Cenderawasih research report on Papuan languages, including Fautngil 2000 and Wafom 2003; the Fautngil abstract may report the stress finding second-hand.

sources.citation: Kim, So Hyun. 2006. (Draft) Survey report on the Sowari language of Papua, Indonesia. Jayapura: SIL Indonesia; 'to appear in SIL Electronic Survey Reports'.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only modern first-hand SIL data on the language (wordlist + sociolinguistics); SIL Papua survey reports sometimes carry a one-line phonology/stress note.

sources.citation: Fautngil, Christ, Robert Masreng & Eti Setiawati. 2000. Fonologi bahasa Demta: laporan penelitian. Jayapura: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa / Jurusan Pendidikan Bahasa dan Seni, FKIP, Universitas Cenderawasih. vi + 87 leaves.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only phonological description of Demta that exists; Pusat Bahasa-funded fonologi reports of this series normally have a 'tekanan' (stress) subsection, so the word-stress statement is almost certainly here.

sources.citation: Cowan, H.K.J. 1952. De austronesisch-papoea'se taalgrens in de onderafdeling Hollandia (Nieuw Guinea). Tijdschrift Nieuw-Guinea 13: 133-143, 160-177, 201-206.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Earliest Demta wordlist with Cowan's notes; Cowan occasionally marks accent in his north-coast wordlists (cf. his Sentani grammar), so it could give an incidental observation.

sources.citation: Maturbongs, Antonius. 2008. Frasa bahasa Demta. Kibas Cenderawasih (jurnal ilmiah kebahasaan dan kesastraan) vol. 4 (2008) [Cornell/HathiTrust copy coo.31924115553038, search-only].
